subject: B200 fleet: standard driver/CUDA baseline + exceptions + runtime compatibility gate request
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:08 AM PST
Subject: B200 fleet: standard driver/CUDA baseline + exceptions + runtime compatibility gate request

Team — following up with the decision from Infra leadership this morning re: B200 standardization.

Decision (baseline for B200 in Redwood-managed fleet)
- NVIDIA driver: 575.42.02 (R575)
- CUDA userspace/toolkit: 12.4 (container base / runtime image)

Why this baseline
- Aligns with NVIDIA guidance for Blackwell bring-up (kernel module + userspace pairing)
- Reduces variance across regions and avoids “works on one rack” issues during profile pack rollout

Exceptions policy (near-term)
We will have a small number of early-access nodes that are not on the baseline for ~2–3 weeks due to vendor imaging + host OS constraints.
- Allowed exception combo (limited): driver 570.xx + CUDA 12.3
- Scope: smoke + benchmark-lab only; not eligible for Hosted production traffic; Dedicated only if explicitly approved by Infra + SRE
- Sunset: target to eliminate exceptions by end of Feb (we’ll send an update once the last rack is re-imaged)

Request to Runtime (profile pack / runtime-1.22)
We need a hard compatibility gate for B200 so we don’t silently run “best guess” configs on unsupported driver/CUDA combos.
- Runtime should detect: SKU=B200 + driver version + CUDA userspace version
- If not on allowlist for the selected profile_version, runtime should refuse to start serving and emit a clear error (including detected versions + expected baseline)
- For early-access exception nodes, we can add an explicit allowlist entry, but ONLY when profile_version is pinned (no default auto-selection)

Operationally, this gives SRE a safe failure mode and makes the profile pack behavior deterministic across the fleet.

Connor: please assume the baseline above for the runtime-1.22 release train messaging. Mateo/Noah: can you confirm ownership on the compatibility gate implementation and where it’s wired in (startup vs model-load)?

Thanks,
Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Infra/SRE Sponsor, Redwood Inference


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: B200 fleet: standard driver/CUDA baseline + exceptions + runtime compatibility gate request

Got it.

We’ll take this on in Runtime. Proposal:
- Hard gate at process startup (before accepting traffic) for SKU=B200.
- Also re-check at model load (defensive) since we’ve seen mixed pools in Dedicated.
- For the exception path: require explicit profile_version pin + “allow_unsafe_compat=false” default; we’ll only enable the 570/12.3 pair via a specific allowlist entry tied to the pinned profile version.

Noah and I will sync today on where the detection lives (we already have driver version extraction wired for H100 selection logic; we’ll extend for B200).

Neha/Irene: can you confirm whether we should treat “unknown CUDA userspace” as fail-closed for B200? (I’d strongly prefer yes.)

Mateo


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 1:05 PM PST
Subject: Re: B200 fleet: standard driver/CUDA baseline + exceptions + runtime compatibility gate request

Thanks Neha — super helpful.

For runtime-1.22:
- I’ll add this baseline to the go/no-go checklist under “B200 readiness” (compat gate must be in place).
- Can you send a one-liner that I can paste into release notes / upgrade notes? Something like “B200 requires driver >= 575.42.02 and CUDA 12.4; runtime will refuse to start on unsupported combos unless explicitly pinned.”

Also: for Private installs, do we want to message this as a recommendation or a requirement? (I’m assuming requirement for “supported”.)

Connor


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 2:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: B200 fleet: standard driver/CUDA baseline + exceptions + runtime compatibility gate request

Connor — wording you can use:

“B200 support is standardized on NVIDIA driver 575.42.02 (R575) and CUDA 12.4. On B200, the runtime enforces a compatibility gate and will refuse to serve on unsupported driver/CUDA combinations. Temporary exception combinations (e.g., 570.xx + CUDA 12.3) are permitted only for early-access bring-up when an explicit profile_version is pinned.”

Re: Private
- Requirement for ‘supported’ B200 profile pack behavior.
- We can phrase it as “supported baseline” and have installer/runtime warn+block (unless the customer explicitly overrides and accepts unsupported). But support stance should be: if you’re off baseline, you’re in best-effort territory.

Mateo question: yes, fail-closed for “unknown CUDA userspace” on B200. If we can’t positively identify, we should assume unsafe.

Neha


From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 4:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: B200 fleet: standard driver/CUDA baseline + exceptions + runtime compatibility gate request

+1 to fail-closed.

A few data points from fleet side so Runtime can encode the guardrail cleanly:
- The exception nodes are only in benchmark-lab and a single staging pool this week.
- We expect to see both 575.42.02 and 575.51.* during the transition (minor patch rev) depending on when racks get imaged. Suggest allowlist “>= 575.42” within R575, not a single exact build.
- For the 570.xx nodes: treat as “bring-up only” and require explicit pin (agree with Mateo’s plan).

Vanessa and I will keep the instance metadata mapping updated so runtime sees a consistent SKU string (B200 SXM vs PCIe should not matter for this gate).

Irene
